title: Agent map
description: Explore the repository, see what is ready, and find the source behind each item.

entries.title: Repository overview
entries.summary: Purpose, current scope, and the boundary between public source and local state.
when: You are new to this repository.
You need to decide whether a file belongs in public Git.
entries.usage: Read README.md before adding or distributing content.
behavior: Explains which areas are implemented and which remain planned.
Lists what can be committed and what must stay local.
outputs: A shared understanding of scope and publication boundaries.

entries.title: Maintenance instructions
entries.summary: The single source of instructions for agents working on this repository.
when: You are changing this repository's structure or content.
You are researching policies, skills, or MCP integration.
entries.usage: Follow AGENTS.md while maintaining this repository.
behavior: Requires active primary-source and individual-workflow community research; maintainer preference is a tie-breaker.
Keeps repository maintenance instructions separate from distributed policy content.
Requires verification appropriate to the change.
outputs: A scoped, researched change with observable verification.

entries.title: Claude entry point
entries.summary: Imports the canonical maintenance instructions without duplicating them.
when: You are working on this repository with Claude Code.
entries.usage: CLAUDE.md imports @AGENTS.md; edit the rules in AGENTS.md.
behavior: Provides a client entry point to the same instruction source.
Contains no independent maintenance rules. Client adherence has not been runtime-tested.
outputs: One maintained set of repository instructions.

entries.title: Structure decision
entries.summary: Nine source repositories compared, with revisions and layout tradeoffs recorded.
when: You are proposing a new directory, package, or distribution route.
entries.usage: Read the decision and inspect the relevant upstream sources before changing the layout.
behavior: Keeps initial source directories small and separates them from future client packaging.
Records observed upstream patterns separately from this repository's choices.
outputs: A layout choice with a reviewable rationale.

entries.title: AK SDLC design
entries.summary: Implemented stage-to-skill routing with independently usable methods; broader design rationale retained.
when: You are designing an SDLC skill or its orchestration.
You need the proposed input, output, and parallel implementation contracts.
entries.usage: Read the design and the linked SDLC routing contract. Runtime multi-provider execution remains unverified.
behavior: Routes existing stages to focused methods.
Distinguishes implemented source contracts from future extensions.
outputs: Stage routing, design rationale and implementation boundaries.

entries.title: Maintain this map
entries.summary: Update the catalog, regenerate the viewer, and check that it matches the source.
when: You add, rename, or change a policy, skill, or MCP definition.
You need to update an item's usage, status, or relationships.
entries.usage:
python3 scripts/build_map.py
python3 scripts/build_map.py --check
behavior: Builds a standalone HTML viewer from catalog metadata and the viewer template.
Checks source paths, statuses, relationships, and coverage of reusable content.
Fails a freshness check when the generated HTML differs from its inputs.
outputs: docs/map/index.html, ready to open locally or serve as static documentation.

entries.title: pstack
entries.summary: Priority reference for engineering workflows, task routing, and verification.
when: You are comparing workflow routing, evidence, or client packaging.
entries.usage: Inspect pinned sources and per-skill provenance. Opening the map does not install or activate anything.
behavior: Provides examples of focused workflows and explicit verification practices.
The structure decision records the source revision inspected for this repository's initial layout.
outputs: Research evidence for a scoped local design choice.

entries.title: Matt Pocock
entries.summary: Priority reference for composable skills, clarification, and short feedback loops.
when: You are comparing skill boundaries, catalog organization, or intent clarification.
entries.usage: Inspect pinned sources and per-skill provenance. Opening the map does not install or activate anything.
behavior: Offers examples of small skills and explicit selection of shipped content.
Use its patterns as evidence; do not assume all of its process fits this repository.
outputs: Research evidence for a scoped local design choice.

entries.title: Addy Osmani
entries.summary: Priority reference for lifecycle workflows, packaging, and repository-only instruction scope.
when: You are comparing workflows, entry commands, or skill resource packaging.
entries.usage: Inspect pinned sources and per-skill provenance. Opening the map does not install or activate anything.
behavior: Separates reusable workflows from instructions for maintaining its repository.
The source comparison notes its documented gap between per-skill installs and root-level references.
outputs: Research evidence for a scoped local design choice.

entries.title: Archify
entries.summary: Turn a system, workflow or repository-backed explanation into an interactive HTML diagram, with editable JSON and explicit artifact/browser checks.
when: A design needs a component map, process flow, request sequence, data pipeline or state-transition diagram.
A Mermaid sketch needs a polished explorable presentation, or an existing diagram candidate needs validation and delivery.
entries.usage: Load skills/archify/SKILL.md. Supply the question, diagram scope and relevant source or Mermaid. Read the selected type’s schema and example, then run the packaged finalize command on the complete candidate; doctor is for setup diagnosis.
behavior: Choose architecture, workflow, sequence, dataflow or lifecycle from the question and read that type’s authoring references.
For a real codebase, trace the requested behavior and attach source evidence; use examples for shape rather than copying their facts.
Write a complete typed JSON candidate and retain it beside the HTML in one request-specific folder. Static presentation is the default; motion is opt-in.
Run finalize on the frozen candidate, including the repository root for repository-backed work. It gates schema validation, delivery, strict provenance and real-browser checks.
Repair a failed gate within the documented limits and rerun finalize. Apply triggered layout-review instructions; inspect captures before claiming visual quality.
Deliver the HTML and editable candidate with actual automated, browser and visual-review status.
outputs: An explorable HTML diagram and its editable typed JSON.
A delivery receipt identifying passed gates, failures and the actual extent of visual inspection.

example.situation: A service reads a cache before calling an API, and the team needs to understand both hit and miss paths.
example.youType: Use archify to show the cache-hit and cache-miss request sequence from this repository. Keep it static and retain editable source.
whatHappens: Trace the cache and API paths in source.
Author a sequence candidate that preserves the branches and return values.
Finalize the candidate, handle any required width review and report the checks actually performed.
example.youGet: A checked interactive sequence diagram with editable JSON and a clear verification report.

adaptation_notes: The adopted Archify package retains its upstream method. This explanation describes that pinned package, not newer releases.
A passing finalize receipt is automated evidence; it does not by itself prove perceptual review. Exports and motion are optional viewer capabilities.

entries.title: Architect
entries.summary: Design caller-facing interfaces, data shapes and ownership boundaries, compare consequential alternatives, and record why one design was selected.
when: A new API, module boundary or data shape will constrain future callers.
A consequential design choice has several plausible alternatives.
entries.usage: Load skills/architect/SKILL.md through the host’s available skill mechanism, or read the source directly. Use architect to design the import pipeline and compare meaningful alternatives. Stop at the selected design. Resolve the methods named in the skill before use; invoke conditional dependencies only when their trigger applies.
behavior: Ground the design in intended behavior and the existing subsystem; use how when context is unfamiliar.
Sketch caller usage, types, signatures, state ownership and recovery behavior before filling in implementation.
For consequential choices, use arena with three providers when available and permitted; record actual participation and capability gaps.
Compare interface depth, testability, migration and operational cost; validate disputed claims with focused experiments.
Record the selected design, rejected alternatives and assumptions that must be checked during implementation.
outputs: A selected interface/ownership design with caller examples, rationale and open questions.

example.situation: An import pipeline needs a stable interface for several callers.
example.youType: Use architect to design the import pipeline and compare meaningful alternatives. Stop at the selected design.
whatHappens: Read current import boundaries.
Compare structurally different sketches against the same scenarios.
Select a coherent design and document its tradeoffs.
example.youGet: A design handoff; implementation starts only if already authorized.

adaptation_notes: AK is design-only by default. The reference map describes upstream architect proceeding into implementation.
Three providers is an AK preference for consequential decisions, not a universal pstack requirement.

entries.title: Arena
entries.summary: Run independent candidates against a frozen task, have a fresh judge compare them, and verify a coherent result assembled from the best compatible ideas.
when: A design or artifact is expensive to change later and independent alternatives are useful.
You need evidence for a choice rather than several variations from one ongoing conversation.
entries.usage: Load skills/arena/SKILL.md through the host’s available skill mechanism, or read the source directly. Use arena to compare cache-key designs against the same migration and correctness constraints.
behavior: Freeze the brief, input revisions, acceptance gates, comparison criteria and budget.
Give each candidate its own output location and the same brief; keep candidate outputs independent.
Collect stable artifacts and record dropouts; a fresh read-only judge compares them against the frozen criteria.
The lead reads the candidates, resolves disagreements using evidence, selects a base and integrates only compatible improvements.
Verify the combined artifact; a winning candidate does not establish that the synthesized result works.
outputs: One verified artifact, participant/coverage record and selection rationale.

example.situation: A cache-key design will be difficult to migrate later.
example.youType: Use arena to compare cache-key designs against the same migration and correctness constraints.
whatHappens: Produce independent candidate designs.
Compare them with a fresh judge and source evidence.
Select a base, incorporate compatible ideas and test the combined design.
example.youGet: A justified choice with actual checks and any capability gaps.

adaptation_notes: AK defines shared comparison criteria before dispatch and uses the host’s authorized capabilities; it does not require a fixed candidate count or assume cloud runners.
Selection grants no additional implementation, publication or merge authority.

entries.title: Code Review And Quality
entries.summary: Review a specific change for correctness, readability, architecture, security and performance, returning prioritized findings tied to source and evidence.
when: A diff, local snapshot or PR needs review before integration.
An assigned independent reviewer needs a review method inside its existing context.
A fix, refactor or dependency upgrade needs its behavior, structure and verification story checked together.
entries.usage: Load skills/code-review-and-quality/SKILL.md. Provide the candidate base/head or snapshot, diff, requirements, repository standards, test evidence and prior findings. State the review-only endpoint and any required finding schema.
behavior: Pin the candidate and scope; distinguish task requirements from repository standards and record missing inputs.
Read the tests first to understand intended behavior, edge cases and whether the checks would detect a regression.
Inspect implementation across the five review axes, including relevant bundled security/performance checklists and dependency changes.
Prioritize concrete defects and structural regressions. Give each finding a location, evidence, impact and an actionable remedy; keep style preferences distinguishable from blockers.
Where authorized and useful, test a defect hypothesis in an isolated disposable copy. Separate checks actually run from author-reported results and inspection-only conclusions.
Return findings, candidate identity and verification limits using the coordinator’s schema when supplied. Review does not edit the author’s work or launch another reviewer.
outputs: A candidate-specific review with prioritized, actionable findings and explicit verification gaps.
Requirement and quality assessments that the author or coordinating workflow can evaluate without guessing the evidence.

example.situation: A retry change passes its happy-path test but may write a payment event twice.
example.youType: Use code-review-and-quality on this pinned diff. Check retry correctness and the regression coverage; return findings without modifying the author’s work.
whatHappens: Compare the retry contract with the tests and implementation.
Trace repeated requests and inspect the deduplication boundary.
Report a demonstrated defect or explain why the hypothesis does not hold, with exact verification limits.
example.youGet: An evidence-backed review of the actual candidate, rather than an unqualified approval.

adaptation_notes: AK uses this method standalone or within the reviewer context already selected by SDLC. Provider selection, shared roles, fallback, publication and re-review belong to the coordinator.
Bundled checklists replace unavailable specialist skills. Experiments stay isolated; an approving review grants no edit, publication, merge or deployment authority.

entries.title: Domain Modeling
entries.summary: Make domain vocabulary precise and record settled meanings in a glossary, with ADRs for consequential tradeoffs that need durable rationale.
when: The same word means different things to different people or contexts.
A domain relationship needs concrete edge-case scenarios.
An agreed term or consequential decision needs a glossary entry or ADR.
entries.usage: Load skills/domain-modeling/SKILL.md through the host’s available skill mechanism, or read the source directly. Use domain-modeling to distinguish login, customer and billing account concepts and document the agreed terms.
behavior: Read existing vocabulary and any context map; surface conflicts instead of silently redefining terms.
Challenge vague concepts with specific scenarios and cross-check claimed behavior against code.
Write resolved meanings immediately in the relevant glossary, keeping implementation details out.
Create files only when there is material to record.
Offer an ADR only for a hard-to-reverse, surprising choice made between real alternatives.
outputs: Clearer canonical terms and the justified glossary/ADR updates.

example.situation: Account currently refers to a login, a customer and a billing relationship.
example.youType: Use domain-modeling to distinguish login, customer and billing account concepts and document the agreed terms.
whatHappens: Find the existing meanings and code usage.
Test boundaries with concrete scenarios.
Update the correct glossary and add an ADR only if its criteria apply.
example.youGet: Precise vocabulary without turning the glossary into a specification.

adaptation_notes: The adopted skill supports multiple domain contexts through GLOSSARY-MAP.md. Merely reading a glossary is not a reason to run this workflow.

entries.title: Grill Me
entries.summary: Sharpen an idea through the grilling interview method without adding the domain-documentation workflow.
when: A plan or consequential decision needs a focused interview.
You want clarification in the conversation rather than glossary and ADR work.
entries.usage: Load skills/grill-me/SKILL.md through the host’s available skill mechanism, or read the source directly. Use grill-me to clarify the export feature. Keep this to an interview. Resolve the methods named in the skill before use; invoke conditional dependencies only when their trigger applies.
behavior: Load the grilling dependency and supply the idea, constraints and decisions already settled.
Ask the currently answerable decision frontier with recommendations.
Use answers to expose dependent questions and stop when consequential decisions are resolved or bounded.
outputs: Shared intent and explicit open decisions in the conversation.

example.situation: You have a feature idea but its scope and success criteria are unclear.
example.youType: Use grill-me to clarify the export feature. Keep this to an interview.
whatHappens: Ask actionable scope and outcome questions.
Reuse the answers instead of restarting the interview.
Summarize settled intent and material unknowns.
example.youGet: A clearer brief, without automatically starting implementation.

adaptation_notes: AK can use this lightweight wrapper early in repository work too; a repository does not automatically require grill-with-docs.
The wrapper adds no glossary/ADR workflow. The shared grilling endpoint still controls what follows.

entries.title: Grill With Docs
entries.summary: Combine the grilling interview with active domain modeling so agreed terminology and consequential decisions remain available after the conversation.
when: Clarifying a change also requires durable domain vocabulary or decision records.
An interview exposes overloaded terms that should be resolved in the project glossary.
entries.usage: Load skills/grill-with-docs/SKILL.md through the host’s available skill mechanism, or read the source directly. Use grill-with-docs to clarify team billing and preserve agreed domain terms. Resolve the methods named in the skill before use; invoke conditional dependencies only when their trigger applies.
behavior: Load grilling for the decision interview and domain-modeling for vocabulary and durable records.
Ask currently answerable questions while checking factual claims against available source.
Record agreed terms in the appropriate glossary and only qualifying tradeoffs as ADRs.
Hand settled intent onward only within the requested scope; the wrapper does not create tickets or start code.
outputs: Shared intent plus justified glossary and ADR updates.

example.situation: Team means a workspace in one module and a billing group in another.
example.youType: Use grill-with-docs to clarify team billing and preserve agreed domain terms.
whatHappens: Interview the consequential choices.
Check the two meanings against code and concrete examples.
Record agreed vocabulary and any justified decision rationale.
example.youGet: A clearer plan with durable domain records, ready for an appropriate handoff.

adaptation_notes: AK selects this wrapper when documents are needed, rather than requiring it at the start of every change.
Do not turn an interview into automatic spec publication, ticket creation or implementation.

entries.title: Grilling
entries.summary: Interview the currently answerable frontier of a decision tree, using recommendations and evidence to resolve consequential assumptions.
when: You want to stress-test a plan, decision or idea.
Another workflow needs the interview method without imposing a documentation wrapper.
entries.usage: Load skills/grilling/SKILL.md through the host’s available skill mechanism, or read the source directly. Use grilling to stress-test the export plan and ask only questions whose prerequisites are settled.
behavior: Map decisions and their prerequisites so dependent questions wait for earlier answers.
Ask the current frontier in a numbered round with recommended answers; a yes accepts the recommendation.
Find environmental facts from available sources instead of asking the user to do that research.
Recompute the frontier after answers and reuse decisions already established.
Finish when consequential choices are resolved or bounded and no material assumption remains hidden.
outputs: A shared understanding of decisions, constraints and bounded unknowns.

example.situation: An export feature has unresolved audience, format and access requirements.
example.youType: Use grilling to stress-test the export plan and ask only questions whose prerequisites are settled.
whatHappens: Ask the current decisions with recommendations.
Wait for answers before asking dependent questions.
Resolve or explicitly bound the material unknowns.
example.youGet: A decision-ready brief, not an unlimited questionnaire.

adaptation_notes: AK stops at consequential readiness rather than literally exhausting every imaginable question.
A finished interview does not grant implementation authority or require another approval of already settled decisions.

entries.title: How
entries.summary: Trace a subsystem from its real entry points to state changes, ownership and failure paths before changing unfamiliar code.
when: You need to understand code before editing it.
You need to locate the owner of an interface, state transition or subsystem boundary.
entries.usage: Load skills/how/SKILL.md through the host’s available skill mechanism, or read the source directly. Use how to trace notification deduplication and subscriber lookups. Keep this investigation read-only.
behavior: Bound the question and identify the relevant source revision.
Read directly for a narrow question; use independent read-only angles only when useful delegation is supported and authorized.
Trace inputs, execution, state ownership and failure paths; distinguish observed behavior from inferred rationale.
Resolve contradictory findings against source and write an explanation with file pointers and remaining gaps.
outputs: A source-backed explanation of the requested flow, relevant files and unresolved questions.

example.situation: You need to change notification deduplication in an unfamiliar service.
example.youType: Use how to trace notification deduplication and subscriber lookups. Keep this investigation read-only.
whatHappens: Find the delivery entry point and state owner.
Trace duplicate checks and subscriber queries.
Explain the flow with source pointers and any unverified performance assumptions.
example.youGet: A traceable investigation, without an implementation claim.

adaptation_notes: AK permits direct or sequential investigation; it does not require a fixed explorer count, cloud runner or an unbundled why skill.

entries.title: Issue Writing
entries.summary: Compose a concise issue that explains the problem, required changes and observable completion criteria so an implementer can start with the available context.
when: An issue, ticket or bug report needs to be drafted, created or rewritten.
An existing issue body no longer expresses the agreed scope or has vague, duplicated completion criteria.
entries.usage: Load skills/issue-writing/SKILL.md and policies/issue-workflow.md. Supply the agreed problem, scope, relevant evidence, destination conventions and whether the requested result is a draft or an authorized tracker update.
behavior: Establish the current agreed goal and required changes, preserving earlier decisions and relevant context.
Write Problem / Goal, Required changes and Completion criteria. Add reproduction or background only when implementation depends on it.
Choose observable outcomes an agent can verify. Consolidate duplicate evidence and keep implementation steps out of the completion checklist.
Reread as a first-time implementer: the problem, work and done conditions must be understandable without extra explanation.
Return the draft or use the shared issue workflow policy for an authorized write, conflict reconciliation and result verification. Body composition does not itself authorize comments or closure.
outputs: An implementation-ready issue body or local draft with concrete completion criteria.
For authorized publication, a verified tracker record and its identifier/link; otherwise an explicit draft status.

example.situation: An export bug report says only “downloads are broken,” but reproduction shows that an empty result returns an error.
example.youType: Use issue-writing to draft an issue for empty exports. Include the reproduction and checkable completion criteria; keep it local.
whatHappens: State the observed failure and intended empty-export behavior.
Describe the required behavior change and the evidence needed to establish it.
Remove process-only checklist items and return the finished draft.
example.youGet: A focused issue that an implementer can act on without an automatic tracker write.

adaptation_notes: This is an AK-authored method released for public reuse; it is not attributed to either reference map.
The shared issue workflow policy owns updates, comments, handoff, closure and safe publication. This skill owns issue-body composition.

entries.title: Planning And Task Breakdown
entries.summary: Turn settled requirements into verifiable end-to-end tasks, explicit dependencies and coherent PR boundaries with clear ownership and handoffs.
when: A spec is ready but implementation order, task ownership or reviewable PR boundaries are unclear.
Parallel implementation is possible and needs independent write scopes, shared contracts and integration checks.
A wide refactor needs a safe migration sequence and complete coverage of existing commitments.
entries.usage: Load skills/planning-and-task-breakdown/SKILL.md with the selected spec, design, repository facts and existing plan. Request an assignable task graph and PR boundaries if the endpoint includes PRs; this invocation stops at the plan.
behavior: Inspect requirements and source constraints; resolve discoverable facts and identify consequential decisions that affect decomposition.
Slice work into end-to-end outcomes and establish shared contracts before consumers. For broad refactors, expand compatibly, migrate callers and then remove the old contract.
Give tasks stable IDs, acceptance criteria, dependencies, owned write scopes, checks and integration requirements. Detect cycles and assign connecting paths explicitly.
For PR work, map tasks into coherent merge units with intended bases and separate PR dependencies under the shared PR policy.
Identify the ready frontier, serialize shared writes and name one integration owner plus the checks that release dependent work.
Reuse the existing task-status authority and trace every source commitment, failure scenario and integration boundary to an owner and verification before handing the plan onward.
outputs: An assignable task graph with critical path, parallel opportunities, blockers and verification handoffs.
When applicable, a PR map with coherent boundaries, dependencies and intended bases.

example.situation: A new export API needs a schema, service behavior and UI, while older callers must keep working.
example.youType: Use planning-and-task-breakdown to plan the export change from the agreed spec. Identify safe parallel tasks and reviewable PR boundaries; stop before implementation.
whatHappens: Establish the shared API contract and compatibility sequence.
Assign end-to-end tasks and the owner of each API-to-UI connection.
Separate task blockers from PR base dependencies and attach focused plus integrated checks.
example.youGet: One plan that can drive implementation or ticket drafts without a second decomposition.

adaptation_notes: AK condenses Addy’s planning method and incorporates adopted pstack/Matt handoff ideas. Task size follows coherent behavior rather than a fixed file or line count.
The existing task-scoped plan remains authoritative. to-tickets consumes it when requested; swarm is a later authorized execution option, not an automatic action of planning.

entries.title: Planning With Files
entries.summary: Keep a durable execution notebook so a long task can resume with its current phase, findings, decisions and verification history intact.
when: Research or implementation spans several stages, many tool calls or multiple sessions.
A task needs reliable recovery after context loss, or concurrent tasks need separate planning records.
Existing planning hooks or completion checks need an explicitly selected task record.
entries.usage: Load skills/planning-with-files/SKILL.md. Resolve the selected project and PLAN_ID, reuse that task’s records, and create only missing planning files. Hooks and optional gated modes require actual host setup; reading the package does not enable them.
behavior: Resolve the selected task before recovery; an invalid explicit selector or ambiguous plan selection must not silently switch to another task.
Maintain task_plan.md for phases and decisions, findings.md for research, and progress.md for actions, errors and verification.
Read the selected record before major decisions and update it as work progresses. Record failures and change the approach rather than repeating an unchanged attempt.
Keep one plan owner when agents collaborate; workers use assigned files or ledgers. Independent tasks need their own host binding or worktrees.
Recover from project planning files by default. Access to same-project host session records requires an explicit metadata or bounded replay request.
Use optional hooks, attestation and completion modes only through the documented host setup; report actual support rather than assuming every host can enforce a gate.
outputs: A task-scoped notebook that makes the goal, current phase, findings, completed work and next action recoverable.
An explicit progress and verification history without automatically reading host transcripts.

example.situation: An investigation will span several sessions, and another task already has an unfinished plan in the repository.
example.youType: Use planning-with-files to keep a separate notebook for the export investigation and resume from it next time. Preserve the other task’s plan.
whatHappens: Resolve or create the intended task record and establish its selection.
Record phases, research and progress in their respective files.
On resume, read that selected notebook and continue from the recorded next action.
example.youGet: Continuity for the investigation without mixing another task’s history into it.

adaptation_notes: The adopted package retains its upstream method. Its notebook complements task decomposition; it does not create another set of PR boundaries or replace tracker-owned status.
Host hooks, plugin commands and gated modes are installation-dependent. A tool subprocess setting PLAN_ID does not bind an already-running parent host’s hooks.
Selected pinned POSIX account hooks are delivered by the account installer; native trust and event execution still require target-client verification.

sources.label: Selected hook source and delivery boundaries

entries.title: Screenshot Manual
entries.summary: Turn real user journeys and sanitized screenshots into an editable step-by-step manual and a PDF checked page by page.
when: A feature or UI change needs instructions that show users the actual controls and results.
An existing screenshot manual is stale after a product change.
Supplied screenshots need a readable manual with their capture and verification limits stated.
entries.usage: Load skills/screenshot-manual/SKILL.md. Supply the audience, goal, product revision and scenarios plus an authorized capture environment or known screenshots. Use the packaged JSON example, build_manual.py and render_pages.py in an isolated Python environment with the declared dependencies.
behavior: Reuse project verifier feature/scenario IDs and user paths when available; reuse captures only when their revision and scenario still match.
Walk the actual product journey and capture useful controls and outcomes within authorization. Use synthetic data and inspect every screenshot for private content.
Write editable JSON with prerequisites, user actions, expected results and specific captions in the audience’s language; retain screenshots beside the source.
Build the PDF with the packaged script and a compatible font for non-ASCII content. Keep draft outputs in the destination’s local artifact area until reviewed.
Extract text and page count, render every page and visually inspect labels, cropping, layout, glyphs and captions. Repair and rerender when needed.
Deliver the PDF, source and sanitized screenshots with the product revision, scenarios exercised and checks actually performed.
outputs: A readable PDF plus editable JSON and sanitized screenshots.
A verification summary separating observed product behavior, screenshot context, build checks and page-by-page visual inspection.

example.situation: Users need to learn how to find an export and download it after the UI changes.
example.youType: Use screenshot-manual to document finding and downloading an export in the current test app. Use synthetic data and deliver the editable source and a visually checked PDF.
whatHappens: Follow the two user actions on the actual app and capture the relevant states.
Write concise steps and expected results tied to the current revision.
Build the PDF, inspect every rendered page and correct unreadable screenshot labels.
example.youGet: A maintainable manual grounded in the actual interface, with honest behavior and visual checks.

adaptation_notes: This workflow and its scripts are original to this repository. The reference maps inform the explanation format, not the manual-generation method.
Screenshots prove visible states, not the entire workflow. Product behavior and PDF visual quality require separate checks; publication is not implicit.

entries.title: Sdlc
entries.summary: Coordinate an authorized task from intent to verified handoff, choosing focused skills for each applicable stage and preserving evidence, review history and endpoint limits.
when: Repository work has an authorized PR endpoint and needs coordinated stages, verification, independent review and correction.
An existing SDLC task needs to resume with its evidence and unresolved findings intact.
The user explicitly requests lifecycle management for a local investigation or implementation; ordinary non-PR work can use focused skills directly.
entries.usage: Load skills/sdlc/SKILL.md and its stage-to-skill routing. Establish review-only, plan-only or implementation scope and a local, PR, pre-merge or main endpoint. Use its state CLI only when the lifecycle is applicable and persistence is authorized.
behavior: Read repository instructions, existing changes and task records; select scope, acceptance outcomes and the authorized endpoint without replacing settled decisions.
Reuse one execution notebook and the canonical stage-to-skill routing. Load only methods whose triggers apply, passing source revisions and required handoff evidence.
For applicable stages, record bounded attempts and evidence-backed decisions to proceed, request a consequential human decision or report a blocker. Main alone writes shared state.
Choose comparable design alternatives when warranted; execute independent authorized implementation slices with isolated resources, explicit owners and serial integration.
Verify the combined candidate with the single tdd method or its explicit alternatives, additional integrated smoke and affected documentation/manual checks.

For PR work, select eligible independent reviewers, deduplicate matching required/additional roles and apply code-review-and-quality inside each assigned context. Preserve findings through fallback, correction and renewed review.
Stop at the selected endpoint. Pre-merge means verified readiness without merge authority; an authorized merge requires current head/base and gate checks followed by remote integration verification.
outputs: A task-specific result with traceable intent, decisions, applicable stage artifacts and candidate-bound verification.
For PR endpoints, an actual review/correction record and an accurate readiness or integration report with remaining gaps.

example.situation: A requested export feature needs implementation and a reviewed PR, but merge has not been authorized.
example.youType: Use sdlc to implement the agreed export feature and finish at pre-merge. Include relevant tests, a screenshot manual and independent PR review.
whatHappens: Reuse settled intent, plan the applicable stages and select their focused methods.
Build and verify the integrated candidate, then carry findings through review and correction.
Report readiness at the actual PR head/base and leave merge disabled.
example.youGet: A verified pre-merge handoff, or a precise blocker with retained evidence; never an implied merge.

flows: Independent review and correction for PR
adaptation_notes: AK owns orchestration; focused skills own their methods and can run independently. Non-PR work receives no new lifecycle unless requested.
The PR implementation route has no separate independent-verification stage. Required and additional roles use one assignment/result when their reviewer matches.
Three-provider design is an AK preference when available and authorized. Host capabilities, source delivery, actual execution and deployment are distinct claims.
Reuse evidenced reviewer launch configurations across corrections; diagnose wrapper errors before declaring a provider unavailable. Account-specific exceptions do not replace required gates.

sources.label: Canonical host adapter and runtime contract

entries.title: Swarm
entries.summary: Coordinate independent coverage jobs, experiments or implementation slices, then integrate evidence into one result with explicit gaps.
when: Many independent targets need the same check.
Ready implementation slices have isolated ownership and verified prerequisites.
You want a bounded candidate race; use arena when independent judging and synthesis are needed.
entries.usage: Load skills/swarm/SKILL.md through the host’s available skill mechanism, or read the source directly. Use swarm to check three independent packages with isolated outputs and one evidence-backed report.
behavior: Choose coverage, race or dependency-aware implementation and freeze the worker contract and budget.
Declare inputs, owned outputs, allowed actions, acceptance checks and PASS / ISSUES / BLOCKED return evidence.

entries.title: Test-first behavior
entries.summary: Show that a focused check fails for the intended behavior, make the change, and retain passing evidence that the behavior now works.

behavior: Use the nearest existing harness and caller-visible interface; keep expected results independent of the implementation.
Run the smallest failing check before implementation and confirm it fails for the intended reason.
Make a coherent fix, rerun the check and cover affected neighboring behavior.
If useful refactoring follows, keep checks green; do not add refactoring merely for ceremony.
When test-first is impractical, record the reason, the actual alternative check and the remaining limits.
outputs: Failing-before/passing-after evidence and the change, or clearly labeled alternative evidence.

behavior: Build a test, command or real user journey that observes the reported symptom; separate setup failure from product failure.
Reduce irrelevant inputs while preserving the original reproduction for final verification.
State competing explanations and disconfirming observations; change one variable at a time.
Use focused probes or a debugger, protect sensitive data, and record frequency for intermittent failures.
If implementation is authorized, use tdd for correction, rerun the original path and remove temporary probes.
outputs: A supported cause or bounded unresolved diagnosis, reproduction evidence and any authorized verified correction.

example.youGet: An evidence-backed cause or explicit uncertainty, rather than a guessed fix.

adaptation_notes: AK allows useful source analysis and bounded partial diagnosis; it does not promise a deterministic reproduction for every flaky failure.

entries.summary: Collect synthetic or scoped native metadata with bounded boundary delivery snapshots; inspect capacity, latency and attribution limits.

For performance or source attribution, follow account/observation/capacity.md and the native-observation recipe.
behavior: One selected client registration per account; grants, epochs and records remain owned by the private store.
Claude has five observer callbacks; Codex has four. Planning hooks stay separate. Codex tool-end status remains unknown, including nonzero shell exits.

Read the native.md platform matrix before relying on another environment: each native result is bound to its executed runtime. Historical Linux Codex tools were blocked and Claude authentication was unavailable; synthetic container execution does not qualify live observer delivery. Native child and WSL coverage remain unverified.
Actor/parent identity, effective exposure, completeness and task success stay unknown. Comparative evaluation and automatic promotion remain planned.
SessionStart/Stop snapshots record bounded delivery hashes and gaps; tool events inherit no cached identity and effective exposure stays unknown.

10,000 actual PostToolUse dispatcher subprocesses using synthetic inputs (no boundary probes) passed record/replay/interruption checks on the reference host; p95 48.16 ms met the under-50 ms target on this one reference run; it is not a cross-host guarantee. This does not qualify native scheduling or later model behavior.
outputs: Private metadata, boundary-scoped delivery snapshots, reservation gaps and measured capacity/latency limits.

entries.summary: Diagnose installed setup, verify actual model identity and skill behavior, and test natural spec-to-plan routing; local Paseo is optional.
when: After installation, updates or client upgrades.
A skill is missing, a hook stopped running, or actual installed-skill behavior needs evidence.
entries.usage: Run sh scripts/setup-account.sh doctor; add --native for discovery/trust and --model-smoke --client codex --model MODEL_ID --evidence-dir .local/account-checks/new-run for a real scenario. behavior: Reuse the ownership receipt and check overrides, aliases, competing routes and executables.
Query native clients without a model turn; report changed Codex trust as blocked.
Verify actual model identity, source use, exact CLI examples and unchanged inputs; report native SessionStart recovery per client.

With --scenario routing, choose spec and planning skills from natural requirements, then verify acceptance coverage and task dependencies.
Qualify setup before eval and after deployment; a successful smoke run is not comparative improvement evidence and never activates observation collection.
Triage failures into reviewed reproduction cases; distinguish environment and grader faults from skill behavior before changing source.
When observation delivery is selected, report an expired, revoked or replaced grant as blocked without renewing consent.
outputs: A pass/fail/blocked/skipped report with next actions and explicit coverage.
Private model evidence for selected real runs; no implicit trust, setup repair or MCP authentication.
